questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to stay in Europe, preferably in a city in Southern Europe. Milan in Italy was one of my only options, but this also suited me well. I highly prioritised choosing a city known for good food and a different culture, which I believed Milan could offer. I also wanted the opportunity to travel to other cities both before and during my exchange, and Milan provided many possibilities for this

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I truly had an amazing experience during my exchange. I loved living in Milan and would recommend it to others who may prioritise academic opportunities less. While the exchange was challenging in several ways, including academically, it was everything beyond the studies that had the greatest impact on my exchange experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I remember it being somewhat difficult to find all the necessary information, but I was prepared for this, as I had read that other students found it challenging as well. The university has a long summer break, which meant that information was sent out quite late, though still in time. Overall, there was simply a large amount of new information to process, with many things to organise, places to find, and documents to submit and have approved. I was fortunate to travel and live there with three other friends from the same education, and we supported each other throughout the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a short chat with Massimo when we got our proof of attendance signed. Other than that it was mainly emails we got sent from the institution that guided us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The administration was really busy since so many students go on exchange in Milan. Everything was very confusing in the beginning and not the easiest to figure out but everything ended up being solved.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For us it was easy since we got a recommendation on accommodation from a friends friend, so we went with that. We rented through Italianway. I would really recommend that. They were nice and helpful and have a lot of different apartments around Milan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: We didn't live that close to our campus but more towards west of the center. You can easily live further away since the metro system is cheap and easy (except when on strike). Maybe check if there is a metro connection from the housing to the campus before.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont know if this reflects the general housing available, but we lived an amazing place and also had some friends that lived in apartments from the same renter.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration of courses was okay to figure out. The difficult part was figuring out which courses existed and their schedule, start, ending time, exam type and more. The schedules are released very close to beginning of the semester do difficult to know if you can take different courses together

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can an Email with a guide. This is okay to follow, but it was unclear if you actually was enrolled to the course. I remember that to some courses i wrote to the professors so they could enroll me if they were locked or something. It is easy to communicate with the professors, just write to them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Im not sure. Not a lot but maybe you could have written to
unimi.in
? But they were busy as written.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was 100% successful at the end

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would visit different courses in the introduction weeks before registration to specific courses. You can just show up and listen to the introduction of the courses, hear about exam forms and get a feeling of the professors. This is smart because you can just sign up for the course later in the semester when you know the schedule and exam forms. We had a very though out plan before we went to Milan, but didnt end up like that at all because of schedule overlaps, late exams and locations far away. So we changed the courses on our OLA some weeks in the exchange and that was fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not very impressing or inspirational but i definitely learned something new and it was challenging trying totally new learning forms and adapt to the italian ways.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general the level was fine for me to follow. I think they have less details in their materials and more concepts so fine if you miss something. Some courses i took were build ups of courses from their bachelor that i hadn't had in DK, so we did some self study to follow but it was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They are some differences. They have more scheduled hours on uni and till very late. Every wednesday and thursday we had classes until 17:30. Also they almost only have lectures which are 2 hours long and have no breaks. Sometimes the professors begins later or stop earlier. You dont really know and that is confusing. I found i very hard to concentrate for so long. especially when you had 4 lectures a day so 8 hours. The professors tend to sit down instead of presenting out to the class. This was not so motivational. And also they dont have any problemsolving classes on the side of the lectures and no previous exam sets to practise on.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Cell therapy and gene silencing (7 ECTS), Molecular pharmacology and immunology (6 ECTS), Molecular bioinformatics (6 ECTS) and Genetics, cellular and molecular biology (12 ECTS)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Cell therapy and gene silencing. The professors were the best i had and the only course with some laboratory work so more variation than just lectures. Also a good level to follow but still new topics. Its a mix of cell therapy in laboratories, pharmacological aspects and virology. The exam was also good, a multiple choice and open questions. Molecular pharmacology and immunology had 2 open questions for each part, you had to pass both pharmacology and immunology (so actually 2 exams). One of the teachers spoke italian english so i didnt understand anything. Both parts were interesting though. Molecular bioinformatics was very boring to me. The exam was multiple choice and open questions for 1 hour. Genetics, cellular and molecular biology easy to follow since it reminds a lot of courses from out bachelor in DK. One of teachers were a little scary and the exam as well. It was verbal and in front of fellow students but this is very common in Italy

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Skitrip 6000. Had to get an italian phonenumber and data. Labcoat 350.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
More expensive was fitness. Actually impossible to do. They only have yearly or half years memberships but you need medical check and so much. 
Less expensive was local transportation, groceries, busses to other cities, coffee.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really experience this so much.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They could have had a students fitness of some sort but our campus didnt offer that. They have a tuesday bar - Tipsy. I went there once and cheap aperol.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visit a lot of restaurants since it is a lot cheaper and more fun than in DK. Visit museums and markets (Remira marked was a personal favorite). Travel to nearby cities, Genova and the coast was nice in the summer. Skitrip also. China town has good food.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The same as above

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took me some time since i like structure and breaks throughout the day. They dont really care so much about that. You just have to relax and hope that everything ends up working out because it will even though there is a lot of uncertainty. The cheap coffee was easy to adjust to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask if they want to have apperitivo with you. They drink aperol all time at the day. We socialised the most in our laboratory class since we were put in random groups so maybe take courses that do that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some exams are very loose and some are kind of nerve-racking. Our professor just handed out the exam 10 minutes before the actual start and told us to begin. But people were still arriving and some even came 10 minutes late but got extra time. Those 20 minutes i couldnt concentrate at all. All the written exams are by hand. The verbal exams are often in front of your class mates. Everyone meets at the same time in the morning and then "først til mølle" princip. I ended up as on of the last student so i sat in the class room for 4 hours without lunch. Remember snacks.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Its a love hate relationship for me at least with their looseness and uncertainty. They are just more relaxed and dont stress so much about what should happen next which was a good practise for me to experience. In general they are just more out in the city enjoying every days of the week eating out, drinking wine, aperitiv ect. Doesnt matter if its monday or friday they drink wine and chat.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be patient with the registration process and choosing courses. Try to shop a bit in the beginning before choosing your final courses. 
Take initiative to meet other people, even if it is just other danish people. It kind of feels like friend dating and is a bit challenging but worth all the effort.
Eat out a lot, drink drinks, visit nearby cities, try new things. Find people who want to share same experiences as you. Their cinemas are so cheap (6 euros) but remember to find version original to get english and not italian. Apollo club was a fun night club.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very different when the masters begin on different campuses. We had courses from 1st october and the laste exam 29th of january. Some other KU student began mid september and ended in december. So we had a whole extra month in Milan which was good and bad depending on your situation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new friendships i got and all the memories we made together. There is something really special about sharing new experiences and living in a new city with people that makes you very close.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to adapt to all the differences. Being "omstillingsparat" when things didn't go as planned or hoped. Also i went on my first skitrip which was challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
